name: Fence the Fox
description: Place fences on a procedural hex field, observe the newly revealed route-priority wind after each fox move, and adapt until every escape route is closed.
natural_language: Cut every escape route before the fox reaches the glowing rim. You have five stakes. After each placement the fox takes a shortest path, following the current visible wind order for route ties, then favoring more shortest onward options and more open neighbors. Observe the newly revealed order before placing again.

metadata.source_notes: Original axial-hex pursuit-evasion implementation grounded in gamedesign.jp's Chat Noir record and the surveyed BFS/minimax solver family. No source code, art, layout, or assets are copied.
metadata.notes: The generator searches each seeded board against a per-turn route-priority sequence and exhaustively certifies shortest depth on radius-three fields. At least one post-initial canonical response on multi-turn boards depends on a wind order revealed only after earlier interaction, so one initial screenshot does not contain the complete future decision state. Full input uses a generated held stake-driver path rather than a one-shot drag. Radius-four profiles retain bounded-search wins without claiming global minimality. The browser, server grader, and exported verifier independently replay the same graph, revealed wind, placement, and gesture contract.
